papers.title: REM sleep suppression after penetrating traumatic brain injury is associated with alterations in the supramammillary-hippocampal circuit.
papers.summary: In a rat model of penetrating traumatic brain injury (pTBI), pTBI suppressed REM sleep and REM-associated theta oscillations and reduced Vglut2 transcript and protein in the supramammillary-hippocampal circuit, with Vglut2 reduction correlating with decreased REM-theta activity. These findings link post-traumatic REM sleep disturbances to dysfunction of the supramammillary-hippocampal glutamatergic pathway.

papers.title: Sleep spindles stabilize human thalamocortical networks, inhibiting pathological disruptions.
papers.journal: bioRxiv : the preprint server for biology
papers.summary: Using multi-night intracranial EEG from 55 epilepsy patients, this study found bidirectional interactions between sleep spindles and interictal epileptiform discharges (IEDs): spindles were associated with IED suppression, while IEDs increased subsequent spindle probability. Nights with fewer IEDs showed more frequent, longer, and faster spindles, suggesting spindles stabilize thalamocortical networks against pathological disruptions.

papers.title: Not all N3 sleep is equal: EEG-defined N3 sleep depth and health-related quality of life in the sleep heart health study.
papers.summary: In 5469 Sleep Heart Health Study participants, shallower N3 sleep (higher odds ratio product during N3) was independently associated with poorer baseline physical and mental health-related quality of life, and with lower follow-up physical quality of life, whereas N3 duration showed no significant associations. The results indicate that EEG-defined N3 depth provides information distinct from N3 duration.

papers.title: One night of closed-loop auditory stimulation during sleep enhances memory consolidation in patients with Alzheimer's Disease.
papers.journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
papers.summary: In a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial of 37 patients with biomarker-confirmed early symptomatic Alzheimer's disease, one night of closed-loop auditory stimulation (CLAS) during sleep significantly improved overnight word-pair consolidation (Cohen's dz = 0.42, p = 0.04) and enhanced stimulation-evoked slow-wave and fast spindle activity without disrupting sleep architecture. This is the first demonstration that CLAS can modulate sleep electrophysiology and improve memory consolidation in AD.

papers.title: Multimodal physiological signal learning for clinical sleep respiratory event recognition.
papers.summary: The paper proposes a multimodal state-space representation learning framework for automatic recognition of sleep-related breathing events, incorporating dual-branch encoders, cross-state token routing, event query prototype fusion, and class-balanced focal margin loss with auxiliary supervision. On the PSG-Audio public dataset it achieved 88.19% accuracy, 84.51% precision, 86.28% recall, and 92.71% AUROC; on a clinical dataset it achieved 74.33% accuracy, 77.51% precision, 84.33% recall, and 90.51% AUROC.

papers.title: Implications of Wearable Sleep Health Technology for Cardiovascular Health Assessment and Interventions: A Narrative Review.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes literature on wearable sleep health technology for cardiovascular assessment and intervention, emphasizing device performance against polysomnography. It reports that wearable devices generally show high sensitivity but lower specificity for detecting sleep versus wake, with multisensor and EEG-based devices approaching polysomnography-level staging, and discusses implications for scalable sleep health measurement in cardiometabolic lifestyle interventions.

papers.title: Structural and Biophysical Basis of Circadian Output Kinase SasA and Its Discrete Stoichiometric Assembly With the KaiC Hexamer.
papers.summary: Determined the crystal structure of the SasA C-terminal ATPase domain from Thermosynechococcus vestitus at 2.31 Å and used mass photometry to show SasA oligomerizes as monomers, dimers, and tetramers, with the KaiC hexamer forming discrete 2:6 and 4:6 SasA:KaiC complexes.

papers.title: Comparison of the Utility of Amplitude-Spectral and Coherence Features of Psychotropic Drugs' Action on ECoG Signal for Pharmaco-EEG Based Drug Screening in Rats.
papers.summary: This study compared the accuracy of a naive Bayesian classifier using amplitude-spectral features, coherence features, or their combination of ECoG signals to classify the pharmacological mechanisms of psychotropic drugs in rats. Combining both feature sets correctly identified 20 of 24 drug groups, outperforming either feature set alone (18 of 24 each) and showing a statistically significant increase in classification accuracy (p < 0.01).

papers.title: Quantum machine learning for detection of sleep deprivation from EEG signals
papers.summary: This study applied Quantum Support Vector Machines and Hybrid Quantum Neural Networks to classify sleep-deprived versus well-rested states from resting-state EEG using spectral band power, band ratios, Hjorth parameters, and functional connectivity features encoded into quantum states. The Hybrid Quantum Neural Network achieved accuracies of 96.88% at the epoch level and 81.25% at the subject level, outperforming previously reported results.

papers.title: Investigating the Link Between Objective Sleep Metrics and Cerebral Small Vessel Disease in a Population-Based Cohort.
papers.summary: In 154 participants from the Hamburg City Health Study, higher proportion of light sleep relative to deep sleep was associated with higher log-transformed PSMD and lower cortical thickness, while REM/non-REM composition and WMH or PVS volume showed no associations.

papers.title: Frequency-Specific EEG burst dynamics in Parkinson's Disease and freezing of gait.
papers.summary: Analyzed resting-state EEG burst dynamics in 237 participants and found that people with Parkinson's disease had more frequent but shorter low-beta bursts at mid-frontal regions versus controls, while FOG severity was most consistently associated with theta burst amplitude metrics.

papers.title: Reassessing Global Field Synchronization as a Phase-Synchrony EEG Metric: Mathematical Review and Empirical Counterexamples With Implications for Wearable Pain Monitoring.
papers.summary: This paper re-evaluates Global Field Synchronization (GFS) as a phase-synchrony EEG metric using mathematical review, synthetic simulations, and empirical resting-state EEG. It found that GFS can dissociate from true phase dispersion (circular standard deviation) under rotations and scaling, and that the expected inverse GFS-CSD relationship was not consistently observed across EEG frequency bands, indicating GFS is not a valid proxy for EEG phase synchronization and limiting its use as a wearable connectivity biomarker.

papers.title: Berberine as a multitarget modulator of metabolic inflammation: molecular mechanisms, circadian regulation, and translational perspectives.
papers.summary: Reviews evidence that berberine modulates metabolic inflammation through interacting pathways including energy sensing, glucose and lipid metabolism, mitochondrial quality control, redox and inflammatory signaling, and gut-liver-microbiota communication, with circadian regulation via BMAL1/CLOCK and REV-ERBα as an underexplored aspect; clinical evidence shows modest benefits for glycemic control, insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, and steatotic liver disease features.

papers.title: SETDB1 cooperates with the CRL4B complex to promote colorectal cancer tumorigenesis by disrupting circadian rhythm.
papers.summary: Shows that SETDB1 interacts with the CRL4B complex to form a transcriptional repressor complex that binds promoters of core clock genes PER3 and CRY1, repressing their transcription, disrupting circadian rhythms, and promoting colorectal cancer cell proliferation, invasion, and stemness.

papers.title: Inter-rater reliability on rhythmic and periodic EEG patterns using Standardized Computer-based Organized Reporting of EEG (SCORE): A multicenter study.
papers.summary: This multicenter study assessed inter-rater reliability (IRR) for rhythmic and periodic EEG patterns (RPPs) using the SCORE system across 10 European centers, with 15 raters evaluating 277 EEG recordings. Overall RPP presence vs absence achieved substantial agreement (κML: .61-.66), individual RPP types reached up to almost perfect reliability (κML up to .98), but posterior dominant rhythm showed low agreement (κML: .06-.47).

papers.title: Pharmacological modulation of hyperarousal in insomnia associated with major depressive disorder: a narrative review of sedating antidepressants and orexin receptor antagonists.
papers.summary: This narrative review examines how heterogeneous insomnia presentations in major depressive disorder may inform the use of sedating antidepressants and dual orexin receptor antagonists (DORAs). It proposes a hypothesis-generating framework, noting that DORAs have the strongest evidence for insomnia disorder, particularly sleep maintenance, but evidence in active MDD remains limited.

papers.title: Clinical efficacy and neurophysiological changes associated with combined transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation and repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation in chronic insomnia disorder: protocol for a randomised controlled trial.
papers.summary: This protocol describes a randomised, double-blind, three-arm controlled trial (n=90) to evaluate whether combined transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) plus repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) yields incremental clinical benefit over either active component alone in chronic insomnia disorder, with primary outcome Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) and secondary neurophysiological measures including EEG, fNIRS, resting motor threshold, and heart rate variability.

papers.title: Melatonin receptor 1 signaling modulates the metabolic response to high-fat diet in female melatonin-proficient mice.
papers.summary: This study investigated the effects of low-fat and high-fat diets on liver biology and transcriptome in melatonin-proficient female mice with MT1 knockout. It found that MT1 deletion alone caused no notable metabolic changes, but combined with high-fat diet led to significant alterations in glucose tolerance, serum lipids, hepatic lipid accumulation, and liver transcriptome, potentially linked to estrogen-related pathways.

papers.title: Attitudes, Strategies and Value Frameworks Guiding Risk Communication in Isolated REM Behaviour Disorder: A Scoping Review of Perspectives From Patients and Healthcare Professionals.
papers.summary: This scoping review analysed 8 articles on risk disclosure for idiopathic/isolated REM sleep behaviour disorder (iRBD). It reports that disclosure of progression risk to α-synucleinopathies is considered essential by patients and professionals but is not consistently integrated into routine practice, with obstacles including prognostic uncertainty, ethical concerns about beneficence, and emotional impact, while patients need comprehensive and trustworthy information.

papers.title: Pancreatic Cancer Disrupts Circadian Patterns of Gene Expression in Cardiorespiratory Muscles.
papers.journal: Journal of cachexia, sarcopenia and muscle
papers.summary: In an orthotopic KPC pancreatic cancer cachexia model, circadian transcriptomes of diaphragm and heart showed that ~60% of rhythmic genes lost rhythmicity in both tissues, with diaphragm disruptions in core clock and metabolic networks and heart loss of rhythmicity in beta-adrenergic/cAMP and insulin response networks, while inflammatory networks gained rest-phase rhythmicity. These findings indicate widespread circadian dysregulation in cardiorespiratory muscles during cachexia.

papers.title: Impact of obstructive sleep apnoea on nocturnal blood pressure: mechanisms and treatment responses - a narrative review.
papers.journal: European respiratory review : an official journal of the European Respiratory Society
papers.summary: This narrative review summarises evidence on how obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) disrupts nocturnal blood pressure control and contributes to nondipping and nocturnal hypertension, and on treatment effects. It reports that continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) has the strongest evidence and lowers nocturnal BP modestly on average, with greater effects in uncontrolled or resistant hypertension and with better adherence, whereas evidence for non-CPAP therapies remains limited and less consistent.

papers.title: Sleep disorders in stroke rehabilitation: mechanisms, impacts, and multidisciplinary management - a narrative review.
papers.summary: This narrative review summarizes the bidirectional relationship between sleep disorders and stroke, reporting that OSA increases stroke risk approximately 2- to 3-fold and post-stroke sleep disorders affect up to 59.9% of patients, with mechanisms including intermittent hypoxia, inflammation, and autonomic dysregulation. CPAP, CBT-I, and rTMS are highlighted as evidence-based management strategies, though high-quality RCTs are needed.

papers.title: Cryptochrome-mediated integration of circadian rhythms into seasonal cycles in the silkworm Bombyx mori.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes recent genome-editing evidence on silkworm cryptochromes BmCRY1 and BmCRY2, showing that Bmcry1 loss disrupts hatching and eclosion rhythms and impairs photoperiodic diapause modulation while temperature-dependent diapause under constant darkness is retained, whereas Bmcry2 mutants show reduced temperature-dependent diapause induction. The findings position cryptochromes at the interface of circadian timing and seasonal developmental control.

papers.title: Monocyte-to-HDL cholesterol ratio in a clinically defined pediatric sleep-related breathing disorder phenotype characterized by witnessed apnea.
papers.summary: This retrospective case-control study compared the monocyte-to-HDL cholesterol ratio (MHR) in 74 children with a clinically defined sleep-related breathing disorder phenotype characterised by witnessed apnea versus 70 controls. MHR was higher in the study group (13.84 vs 10.15; Holm-adjusted p<0.001) and remained associated with group membership after age and sex adjustment (adjusted OR=1.315); adding MHR increased AUC from 0.563 to 0.777, with optimism-corrected AUC 0.762, but MHR is proposed as a complementary research biomarker rather than a diagnostic test.

papers.title: Incremental Prognostic Value of Wearable-Derived Heart Rate and Activity Circadian Features in Tricuspid Regurgitation.
papers.summary: No abstract was available for this paper. Therefore, no summary of the study question, methods, or reported results could be generated from the supplied metadata.

papers.title: Clinical Implementation of Amplitude-Integrated Electroencephalography for Neonatal Seizure Detection and Prognostication: First National Experience From North Macedonia.
papers.summary: This prospective observational study of 64 neonates evaluated amplitude-integrated EEG (aEEG) for seizure detection and prognostication, finding electrographic seizures in 51.5% of clinically suspected cases versus 25.8% of high-risk neonates and showing that abnormal aEEG background was the strongest predictor of adverse neurodevelopmental outcome (OR 9.62, 95% CI 1.38-67.25).

papers.title: Digital distraction and adolescent development: a narrative review of smartphone use, cognitive effects, and policy interventions.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes evidence on adolescent smartphone use and its effects on psychological well-being, cognitive functioning, and school policy responses. It reports that excessive smartphone use is consistently but modestly associated with sleep disruption, reduced attentional capacity, and increased internalizing symptoms, with heterogeneous effects moderated by activity type, timing, and individual vulnerability; school phone bans improve classroom attention and engagement but broader mental health impacts remain unclear.

papers.title: Regulating the Hyperdopaminergic Substrate in Restless Legs Syndrome With Augmentation: An Open-label Study on the Safety and Efficacy of Aripiprazole.
papers.summary: This open-label observational study tested low-dose aripiprazole (5 mg daily) with gradual dopamine agonist tapering in 18 adults with severe restless legs syndrome and augmentation. All patients discontinued dopamine agonists, with significant improvements in IRLS scores, CGI, subjective sleep time, and sleep quality, and only mild transient adverse events.

papers.title: Multi-modal connectome analysis of the stereoelectroencephalography implantation effect: a case report.
papers.summary: This case report used longitudinal multi-modal connectome analysis in a patient with drug-resistant right temporal lobe epilepsy who experienced seizure reduction after stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG) implantation. The findings showed decreased hippocampus-amygdala and fusiform gyrus-temporal pole connectivity, increased hippocampus-posterior cingulate connectivity, reduced connectome eccentricity, and histopathological evidence of lymphocytic infiltration and reactive gliosis around electrode trajectories.

papers.title: When Campus Feeds the Clock: How the University Food Environment Shapes the Circadian Rhythms of Undergraduate Students at the University of Medical Sciences, Ondo
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 302 undergraduate students at a Nigerian medical university assessed how the campus food environment relates to circadian eating patterns, finding that most students had moderate (71.9%) or poor (21.2%) circadian eating patterns and that poor physical food accessibility (AOR 6.44) and poor food policy environment (AOR 9.53) independently predicted poor circadian eating patterns, which were also associated with BMI category.

papers.title: The Gut-Lung Axis in Respiratory Diseases: Mechanisms, Microbiome Dysbiosis, and Therapeutic Implications. A Comprehensive Review.
papers.summary: This comprehensive narrative review synthesized 146 studies to examine the bidirectional gut-lung axis in respiratory diseases, detailing mechanisms such as immune cell trafficking, short-chain fatty acid signaling, vagal neuroimmune communication, and epigenetic regulation, and reviewing microbiome-targeted therapeutic strategies including probiotics, prebiotics, dietary interventions, fecal microbiota transplantation, and vagus nerve stimulation while noting limitations such as predominantly observational designs and limited human mechanistic data.

papers.title: Acute Respiratory Failure Associated with Severe Obstructive Sleep Apnea as an Early Manifestation of Multiple System Atrophy: A Case Report.
papers.summary: This case report describes an 81-year-old woman with multiple system atrophy who developed acute respiratory failure associated with severe obstructive sleep apnea syndrome requiring intubation and subsequent noninvasive ventilation, with polysomnography confirming OSAS and laryngoscopy showing mild bilateral vocal cord abductor paresis without stridor, highlighting that life-threatening respiratory failure may precede laryngeal stridor in MSA.

papers.title: Postoperative pain trajectories and associated factors in patients undergoing lung cancer surgery: a scoping review.
papers.summary: This scoping review mapped 11 studies on postoperative pain trajectories after lung cancer surgery, identifying 35 study-specific trajectory classes grouped into intensity/recovery-based, pain-threshold-based, and context/special-pattern categories, along with 14 assessment tools and associated factors clustered into physiological, surgery-related, analgesic, and cognitive-psychological domains.

papers.title: Current Tobacco Use Status Associated with Insufficient Sleep Duration and Sleep Problems Among Non-Hispanic Black and Hispanic Men with Chronic Conditions.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional survey of 1,673 non-Hispanic Black and Hispanic men with chronic conditions examined associations between tobacco use patterns and sleep outcomes. Exclusive cigarette smokers (AOR=1.43) and dual-tobacco users (AOR=1.56) had higher odds of insufficient sleep, while dual-tobacco users (AOR=1.96) and poly-tobacco users (AOR=1.66) had higher odds of sleep problems compared to non-tobacco users.

papers.title: Cloning of a novel cyanobacterial serotonin N-acetyltransferase gene CySNAT3 and its integration with transcriptomic drug repurposing in pediatric obstructive sleep-disordered breathing.
papers.summary: The study cloned, expressed, and purified a novel cyanobacterial serotonin N-acetyltransferase (CySNAT3) that catalyzes melatonin synthesis, and integrated transcriptomic drug repurposing of pediatric oSDB tonsillar RNA-seq data to identify four candidate drugs with favorable binding to target proteins.

papers.title: Association of Circadian Syndrome with Incident Risk of 23 Site-Specific Cancers: A Large-Scale Prospective Study in the UK Biobank.
papers.summary: This prospective cohort study in 367,832 UK Biobank participants examined associations between circadian syndrome (combining metabolic, sleep, and mood traits) and incident cancer risk. Circadian syndrome was associated with higher overall cancer incidence and the strongest positive associations were for endometrial, liver, and kidney cancers; sex-hormone-binding globulin accounted for 51.0% of the endometrial cancer association and C-reactive protein for 26.4% of the overall cancer association.

papers.title: Individualized perioperative nutritional management in orthognathic surgery: an evidence-graded, integrated framework linking upper-airway change, feeding function, and psychological status.
papers.summary: This mini-review synthesizes evidence on perioperative nutritional management in orthognathic surgery, grading three domains (upper-airway change, feeding function, psychological status) by proximity to nutritional outcomes, and proposes a hypothesis-generating risk-stratified framework highlighting that only feeding function has direct longitudinal support.

papers.title: A rare de novo contiguous 15q11.1-q13.3 duplication with tetrasomy (CN=4) and adjacent trisomy (CN=3) associated with severe global developmental delay, autism spectrum disorder, and subclinical epileptiform discharges: a case report and literature review.
papers.summary: A case report describes a Chinese girl with a rare de novo contiguous 15q11.1-q13.3 duplication comprising a tetrasomic and adjacent trisomic segment, presenting with severe global developmental delay, autism spectrum disorder, and subclinical epileptiform discharges, expanding the genomic spectrum of complex proximal 15q rearrangements.

papers.title: Medication Regimens for Orthognathic Surgery: Comparative Effects on Hemodynamics and Pain Control.
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 171 patients undergoing Le Fort I osteotomy, standardized induction and emergence anesthetic protocols (used together) were associated with the lowest mean arterial pressure upon awakening and significantly lower median and maximum postoperative day 0 pain scores versus conventional management. Tranexamic acid was independently associated with lower intraoperative mean arterial pressure in the control cohort.

papers.title: Mental Health of Early and Prolonged Parent-Child Separated Children in Chinese Immigrant Families: A Qualitative Study With Parent-Child Dyads.
papers.summary: A qualitative interview study with 24 parent-child dyads from Chinese immigrant families examined mental health in children who experienced early and prolonged separation as "satellite babies" sent to China and later reunited with parents. The study reported both negative outcomes (avoidance of disclosure, social withdrawal, externalized and internalized problems, low-quality sleep) and positive mental health conditions (positive general mental health perception, high self-esteem, healthy social engagement, high-quality sleep), indicating within-group mental health disparities.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
